exchanges.note: 2010-2024 sourced from exchange_calendars only (backfill; not independently verified). 2025-2027: exchange_calendars + exchange_publications (the exchange's calendar, published to 2027). 2028-2029: predicted from exchange_calendars and the exchange's unchanged pattern; not yet published, although most entries cite the calendar page. Close-time convention: the registry uses 16:30 (full days) and 12:30 (half days) for 2025-2029, while exchange_calendars uses 16:28 and 12:28 and so do the backfilled 2010-2024 half days (12:28). This is not rounding in the library: Euronext's half-day notice gives Dublin equities a close between 13:28 and 13:30 CET (12:28-12:30 Dublin time), a two-minute window, so the registry holds the end of the window and the library its start. Rechecked 2026-11-19 (4c-R3) against Euronext's trading-hours-and-holidays page and its 2027 holiday calendar. Fixed: (1) 2027-12-28 (Tue) is closed but unconfirmed (maintainer decision, 4c-R3.5, reversing 4c-R3): Irish law moves St Stephen's Day (Sun 26 Dec 2027) to Tue 28 Dec; in 2021, the same weekday layout, Euronext closed Dublin on both 27 and 28 December (Euronext's 2021 holiday-calendar release, which this entry cites); and both exchange_calendars and pandas_market_calendars close it. Euronext's 2027 holiday calendar lists only Mon 27 December, which is the reason for doubt. The 2025-2027 coverage span marks it unconfirmed with recheck_date 2027-11-30: re-check against Euronext Dublin's end-of-2027 notice and open the day only if Euronext says explicitly that it trades. (2) When Dec 24 or Dec 31 falls on a weekend, Euronext Dublin holds the half day on the preceding Friday (2022-12-23, 2022-12-30, 2023-12-22, 2023-12-29 in Euronext's tables); 2028-12-22 and 2028-12-29 added as predicted half days, as exchange_calendars has them. (3) Half-day time convention (4c-R3 decision: close = end of the closing auction): Euronext states Dublin equities close between 12:28 and 12:30 Dublin time on half days (random end), so the close is 12:30, as the 2025+ entries already had; the 2022-2024 half days (12:28 from exchange_calendars) are now 12:30, citing Euronext, whose statement covers those years. Earlier half days: see the 4c-R3.5 close-convention sentence below (2019-2021 12:30, 2010-2018 12:28). The full-day 16:30 is likewise the end of the 16:28-16:30 closing window. Checked, no change: Irish May Bank Holiday closures (2025-05-05, 2026-05-04, 2027-05-03), 2026-12-28 and 2027-12-27 match Euronext; no COVID-19 closure; hours 08:00-16:30 Dublin throughout. Close convention (ADR 0013, 4c-R3.5): half-day close = end of the closing auction. Euronext Dublin moved from the ISE's Xetra (Deutsche Börse) platform to Euronext's Optiq on 2019-02-04 (Euronext press release of 4 February 2019, https://www.euronext.com/en/about/media/euronext-press-releases/euronext-dublin-transitions-irish-listed-companies-optiq), not in 2021 as the 4c-R3 note said. Half days since then: 2019 (24 and 31 Dec): Euronext's trading hours & holidays page, 'Calendar of business days 2019' (https://live.euronext.com/en/resources/trading-hours-holidays), gives Dublin equities closing between 13:28 and 13:30 CET (12:28-12:30 Dublin time) and ETFs at 13:00 Dublin, so 12:30 (4c-R4; 4c-R3.5 had 13:05 from the October 2018 release's 'all instruments closing by 14:05 CET', which is an upper bound, not an auction end); 2020 and 2021: Euronext's holiday-calendar releases give the same 12:28-12:30 Dublin window, so 12:30, as for 2022+. Close (4c8, resolved): Euronext's Appendix to Instructions 4-01/4-03, sheet 'Appendix to 4-01 Manual OPTQ', effective 3 August 2026 (https://www.euronext.com/sites/default/files/2026-07/appendix%20to%20Euronext%20Instructions%204-01%204-03%20Trading%20Manuals_0.xlsx; the version effective 23 November 2026 has the same Dublin rows), gives every Dublin equity trading group in continuous mode (9A, 9B, 9C, 9D, 9F, 9G, 9J, 9O, 9P, and JQ in the November version), in CET: continuous trading '09:00 Random - 17:28', closing uncrossing '17:30 Random' and Trading at Last '17:30 - 17:40'. Its notes define '17:30 Random' as a closing uncrossing that randomly occurs between 17:30:00 and 17:30:30 CET. So 16:28-16:30 Dublin time is the closing call and the scheduled uncross is 16:30 Dublin; regular_hours.close 16:30 is the end of the closing auction under ADR 0013 (the 30-second random end is ignored), and the 4c-R5 question whether the uncross was scheduled at 16:28 is answered no. Half days: the Appendix has no half-day rows (those are in Euronext's end-of-year appendix, not read); Euronext's statement that Dublin equities 'close between 12:28 and 12:30' has the same two-minute closing-call shape, so 12:30 is kept as the half-day uncross. The 2019-02-04 unconfirmed marker is removed. 2010-2018 half days keep exchange_calendars' 12:28: the ISE Xetra era, for which no half-day schedule was found.

hours.note: Manual Operativo, 'Versión 1.97/2026', 'Vigencia a partir del 23 de julio de 2026' (the maintainer's PDF, 107 pages, read directly in 4b6), 1.1.2 'Horario de la Sesión de Remate': 'c) Mercado contínuo para títulos de renta variable, de renta fija y warrants de 8:30 a 15:00 horas.'; 'b) Subastas de Apertura ... de 8:00 a 8:29:59 horas.'; then 'El horario de la Sesión de Remate durante el horario de verano (estacional) en Estados Unidos, para fines de mantener homologado el horario de la sesión de remate de la BMV con el horario del mercado de Nueva York, será el siguiente:' with 'c) Mercado continuo para títulos de renta variable, de renta fija y warrants de 7:30 a 14:00 horas.'; 'Los horarios de inicio de cada etapa ... se aplicarán de manera aleatoria entre la hora señalada y el segundo inmediato siguiente' (seconds of jitter: the stated times). 1.1.3: 'durante el horario de 8:30 a 15:00 horas (7:30 a 14:00 horas durante el horario de verano EUA) de la Sesión de Remate'. So close 15:00, the end of continuous trading; open 08:30. 4b4 read the same manual through WebFetch; this replaces that reading. The maintainer's saved 'Horarios de Negociación' tab gives the US-summer table 'Mercado Continuo 7:30 a 14:00' under a heading 'Anterior' (the English tab labels 8:30-15:00 'Previous', so the heading dates nothing). BMV's avisos page (15 October 2025, 'Homologación de los horarios de operación del Mercado de Capitales con los de EUA'): from Monday 3 November the session 'iniciará a las 8:30 horas para concluir a las 15:00 horas'. Close (ADR 0013): BMV has no closing auction; the closing price is calculated from 'los precios de los últimos 20 minutos de la Sesión de Remate' (1.3.6.6.2) and closing-price orders execute at 15:00; trades at the closing price 15:01-15:19:59 are not regular hours. History: BMV's 2019 manual (V1.67) already gives 8:30-15:00; before 2023 Mexico kept daylight saving time, and BMV shifted only in the weeks the two countries' changes differed (aviso of 15 October 2021: 7:30-14:00 from 1 to 5 November 2021). exchanges.note: 2010-2024 sourced from exchange_calendars only (backfill; not independently verified): 150 closures (146 named) and 28 early closes at 12:45 on the business days before Christmas Day and New Year's Day, 2011-2024 (exchange_calendars' value, the end of continuous trading; ADR 0013 would give 13:00, see below). exchange_calendars has no 2010 abbreviated days; an NZX holiday-period notice for 24 and 31 December 2010 (nzx attachment 131349, seen only as a search snippet) gives abbreviated hours with pre-close to 16:00, not read in full, so 2010 is unchanged. 2025 to 2027-01-04: exchange_calendars + exchange_publications. 2027-01-05 to 2027-12-31 and 2028-2029: standing pattern, predicted (4d2). Checked 2026-11-20 (4c9). Last published year: NZX's memo 'NZX Market Holidays - 2025/2027' (https://www.nzx.com/announcements/463713, NZX Product Operations, Monday 1 December 2025; the attachment, robots-blocked to this sandbox, was saved by the maintainer and read in 4d2). Its table runs from 'Business Day Prior to Christmas Day, Wednesday, 24 December 2025, Abbreviated Trading' to 'Day after New Year's Day, Monday, 4 January 2027, Closed' (footnote: 'As 2 January 2027 falls on a Saturday, the following Monday is observed'): 19 rows, every one matching the registry, including 'Abbreviated Trading' on Thursday 24 and Thursday 31 December 2026, which were predicted and now cite the memo. The memo gives no hours ('For further details about the abbreviated trading hours, please visit: https://www.nzx.com/investing/nzx-trading-hours'), so the 13:00 end stays on the trading-hours source below (ADR 0013). It stops at 4 January 2027: the rest of 2027 (Waitangi Day observed 8 February to the 31 December abbreviated day, 11 rows) is not published and is marked predicted; NZX issues each memo in December for about the next thirteen months, so the 2027 rows are expected in its December 2026 memo. Close (ADR 0013): NZX's 'Anatomy of a trading day' (https://www.nzx.com/services/nzx-trading/anatomy-of-a-trading-day) gives Normal Trading 10:00-16:45, Pre-Close from 16:45, and the closing auction at a random time 30 seconds either side of 5:00pm, then Adjust to 5:30pm. The scheduled close is therefore 17:00 (was 16:45, the end of continuous trading; exchange_calendars has 16:45), as one dated entry from 2010-01-01 (unconfirmed: no earlier schedule was read). Abbreviated trading days: NZX's trading-hours page gives abbreviated days as Normal Trading 10:00-12:45, Pre-Close 12:45-13:00, Adjust 13:00-13:30 (read only as a search snippet of beta.nzx.com's Hours & Boards page; the page itself refuses this sandbox). NZX's 2024/2026 holiday memo (announcement 443000, snippet) lists 31 December 2025 as abbreviated trading, and NZX's announcement 463815 (https://announcements.nzx.com/announcement/463815) says NZX markets operate abbreviated hours on 24 and 31 December 2025. So 2025-12-24 and 2025-12-31 are early closes at 13:00 (the file had none; exchange_calendars has 12:45). 4c10: NZX's own pages re-read. 'Anatomy of a trading day' (https://www.nzx.com/services/nzx-trading/anatomy-of-a-trading-day) again gives the closing auction at a random time between 16:59:30 and 17:00:30, so the 17:00 close stands (ADR 0013). For abbreviated days NZX's own notices (https://announcements.nzx.com/attachment/433988.pdf, 11 December 2024; https://announcements.nzx.com/announcement/463815, 2 December 2025) say NZX markets operate abbreviated hours 'closing at 1.30pm'. That is the end of the session (the Adjust end; on a normal day the same point is 17:30), an upper bound under ADR 0013. The abbreviated-day closing auction at 13:00 rests on NZX's Hours & Boards table (Pre-Close 12:45-13:00), read only as a search snippet because the page renders client-side, so 13:00 is kept as the ADR 0013 convention for 2025-2029 and the 2025 dates are marked unconfirmed for the time. exchange_calendars' 12:45 (end of continuous trading) stays for 2011-2024 as an ADR 0013 exception. The 2026 and 2027 abbreviated days (Dec 24, Dec 31) are in NZX's memo 'NZX Market Holidays - 2025/2027' (https://www.nzx.com/announcements/463713), but its attachment is robots-blocked (api.nzx.com) and was not read. They are therefore added as predicted early closes at 13:00 (dates as in exchange_calendars, which has all of 2025-2029 at 12:45) and stay unconfirmed. 2028 (Dec 22, Dec 29) and 2029 (Dec 24, Dec 31) are added as predicted on the same pattern. exchanges.name: Oslo Børs
exchanges.note: 2010-2024 sourced from exchange_calendars only (backfill; not independently verified). 2025-2027: exchange_calendars + exchange_publications (Euronext's holiday calendar, published to 2027). 2028-2029: predicted from exchange_calendars and Euronext's unchanged holiday pattern; Euronext has not published those years, although the entries cite its calendar page. regular_hours: close 17:30 before 2012-08-06, 16:30 after. Oslo Børs cut trading hours by one hour on 2012-08-06; 16:30 includes the closing auction (continuous trading ends 16:20, which is the single close exchange_calendars has for 2000-2026, so its pre-2012-08-06 hours are wrong). The 17:30 close before the cut is inferred from the one-hour reduction and is dated from the start of the registry, not from a notice. Rechecked 2026-11-19 (4c-R2) against Euronext's trading-hours-and-holidays page. Fixed: the Wednesday before Easter is an Oslo half trading day every year (Euronext lists 2025-04-16, 2026-04-01 and 2027-03-24 as half trading days for Oslo only); exchange_calendars and the 2011-2024 backfill had it, but 2025-2029 did not. Added the three published dates and an easter_offset -4 early_close rule (effective_from 2025-01-01) that also generates 2028-04-12 and 2029-03-28. Half days (ADR 0013): close = the scheduled closing uncross. Euronext's own Oslo Børs half-day schedules give, for cash equities, continuous 09:00-13:00, call 13:00-13:05, uncrossing 13:05, Trading At Last 13:05-13:10, closed 13:10, in every year read: 2023-04-05 (https://www.euronext.com/en/media/7620/download), 2024-03-27 (https://www.euronext.com/en/media/10309/download), 2025-04-16 (https://www.euronext.com/en/media/12510/download), 2026-04-01 (https://www.euronext.com/en/media/14571/download) and 2027-03-24 (https://www.euronext.com/en/media/16430/download). The 2025, 2026 and 2027 production PDFs hold the table as an image; it was read from page renders of copies of the same documents supplied with the 4c-R4 and 4c8 briefs. Those five days are 13:05 (4c-R5 for 2023, 2024, 2026; 4c8 for 2025, 2027), and the easter_offset rule generates 2028-04-12 and 2029-03-28 at 13:05 too, predicted from that pattern (4c8; 4c-R5 had kept 13:00). 2011-2022 keep 13:00, exchange_calendars' value, marked unconfirmed: no readable Euronext schedule (Oslo joined Euronext in 2019; the 2022 schedule, media 4701, could not be read). Dec 24/31 are full closures (rules), as Euronext lists. Hours: no change after 2012-08-06 was found (continuous 09:00-16:20, closing at 16:20 per the 2020 Optiq migration guidelines); no 2020 COVID-19 closure. Close convention (ADR 0013, 4c-R3.5): close = end of the closing auction. Full-day close (ADR 0013, 4c8): Euronext's Appendix to Instructions 4-01/4-03, sheet 'Appendix to 4-01 Manual OPTQ', effective 3 August 2026 (https://www.euronext.com/sites/default/files/2026-07/appendix%20to%20Euronext%20Instructions%204-01%204-03%20Trading%20Manuals_0.xlsx; the 23 November 2026 version agrees), gives every Oslo equity trading group in continuous mode (O1-O9, OA-OH, OO, OT-OY) continuous trading '09:00 Random - 16:20', closing uncrossing '16:25 Random' (randomly between 16:25:00 and 16:25:30 CET, which is Oslo local time) and Trading at Last '16:25 - 16:30'. The close is therefore 16:25, not 16:30 (the end of Trading at Last). regular_hours now reads 17:30 from 2010, 16:25 from 2012-08-06 and 16:25 from 2026-08-03: the last entry is the Appendix's effective date, and 2012-08-06 is marked unconfirmed on the 2010-2024 coverage span because no earlier Euronext or Oslo Børs schedule was read (the one-hour cut of 2012-08-06 and exchange_calendars' 16:20 continuous end are consistent with 16:25). The pre-2012 17:30 remains inferred. The undated regular session shows 16:25 (the latest entry, per the repository rule); post_market and extended_hours.after_hours now open at 16:25 (Trading at Last 16:25-16:30) and keep their 16:45 end.

Last published year: MOM's press release Public Holidays for 2027 (https://mom.gov.sg/newsroom/press-releases/2026/0618-public-holidays-for-2027) lists the 11 gazetted holidays; the registry's 2027 weekday closures (Jan 1, Feb 8, Mar 10, Mar 26, May 17, May 20, Aug 9, Oct 28) match exactly. SGX's own trading-calendar page (sgx.com/trading/trading-hours) could not be read here, so the 2027 half-day dates (Feb 5, Dec 24, Dec 31) follow the standing pattern. Close (ADR 0013): SGX-ST Regulatory Notice 8.2.1 (https://rulebook.sgx.com/node/9044) gives, for normal days, trading 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, a 60-minute Mid-Day Break 12:00-13:00, the Closing Routine with Pre-Close 17:00 to 17:04-05 (random end) and Non-Cancel to 17:06, then Trade at Close 17:06-17:16; for half days, trading 09:00-12:00, Pre-Close 12:00 to 12:04-05, Non-Cancel to 12:06, Trade at Close 12:06-12:16. The closing price is set at the end of the Closing Routine, so regular_hours.close is 17:06 (was 17:00, the end of continuous trading) and half days close at 12:06 (was 12:30). The undated sessions add the lunch_break 12:00-13:00, move the closing auction to 17:06, and post_market and extended_hours.after_hours become Trade at Close 17:06-17:16. Hours history (dated regular_hours, all 09:00-17:06): 2010-01-01 (unconfirmed; no pre-2011 SGX schedule was read; a 12:30-14:00 lunch break applied then), 2011-08-01 (SGX's release 'SGX securities market trades all day from 1 August', https://investorrelations.sgx.com/static-files/9ef0a612-b4bb-4c44-9632-d01f40f206fd; the 2011 Practice Note version gives Non-Cancel 17:05-17:06), and 2017-11-13 (SGX-ST rule amendments of 13 November 2017, https://rulebook.sgx.com/sites/default/files/net_file_store/SGX-ST_November_13_2017.pdf, which add the 12:00-13:00 Mid-Day Break and move the half-day Closing Routine from 12:30-12:36 to 12:00-12:06). The schema cannot date a lunch break, so the 2011-2017 continuous session is described here only. Half days 2028-2029 (4c9): 2028-01-25, 2029-02-12, 2029-12-24, 2029-12-31 moved from 12:30 to 12:06 and are predicted, following the confirmed 2025-2027 pattern. Close window (4c9): Regulatory Notice 8.2.1 paragraph 3.6(a) says Trade at Close begins after the Closing Routine ends at 17:06 (12:06 on half days). Only the Pre-Close end and the Non-Cancel start are random (17:04-17:05, 12:04-12:05). So 17:06 and 12:06 are the fixed scheduled ends of the closing auction, which is what ADR 0013 uses.

Holiday creation dates: exchange_calendars follows the 2019 amendment of the Croatian holidays act (in force 2020): Independence Day (8 October) closes only to 2019, Statehood Day moves from 25 June (to 2019) to 30 May (first weekday 2022), and Remembrance Day (18 November) starts in 2020; nothing is closed before its law, so nothing is removed. The act itself was not re-read in 4c11. Corrections: 0. 2025-2027: exchange_calendars + exchange_publications. 2028-2029: standing pattern. Checked 2026-11-20 (4c11). Last published year: ZSE's non-trading days page (https://zse.hr/en/non-trading-days/110) lists 2026 and 2027, and the 'Trading calendar in 2027' post of 9 September 2026 (https://zse.hr/en/trading-calendar-in-2027/3574) lists the 2027 days; the registry's 2026 and 2027 weekday closures match both exactly (their existing citations are kept). Close (ADR 0013): ZSE's Trading Manual of 14 January 2026, in force 22 January 2026 (https://zse.hr/UserDocsImages/docs/trading/manuals/Trading_Manual_2026-01-14.pdf), gives for Continuous Trading: pre-trading 08:00-09:00, opening auction 09:00-09:30, continuous trading 09:30-12:00, intraday auction 12:00-12:10, continuous trading 12:10-15:55, closing auction 15:55-16:00 (earliest ending; the end is random, up to 15 seconds later), trading at close 16:00-16:10 and post-trading 16:10-16:25. ADR 0013 ignores the random window, so the close is 16:00, unchanged (the file and exchange_calendars both have 16:00); the open stays 09:30, the start of continuous trading (exchange_calendars has 09:00, the opening auction). One dated entry from 2010-01-01, unconfirmed: the manual is the 2026 version; the 2017 Xetra T7 migration and the December 2019 schedule were read only through custodian newsflashes.
